jurisdiction.name: Serbia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Serbia steers AI through Government strategies, institutions and non-binding ethics guidance. The AI Development Strategy 2025-2030, adopted in January 2025, replaced the 2020-2025 strategy and announces a dedicated AI law, which is still being drafted. The Government founded an AI Research and Development Institute in 2021, set up an AI Council in 2024 and adopted ethics guidelines for reliable and responsible AI in 2023. The only binding rule so far is article 38 of the GDPR-aligned Law on Personal Data Protection, on decisions made solely by automated processing; a 2026 Ministry of Justice draft of a new data protection law adds AI-specific rules on risk tiers, transparency and labelling of synthetic content. The standards institute has adopted ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 22989 as national standards. Serbia is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
lead_institutions: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 13 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass the same day, covering the official gazette register, all 101 bills before the National Assembly, all 673 topics on the Government's consultation portal, each ministry and each sector regulator. Not yet verified from the official text: possible deepfake provisions in three Criminal Code bills and an electronic media bill, which are scanned without text, and material from the health, justice and agriculture ministries. The planned AI law, the e-Government Programme 2026-2030 proposal and the media regulator's 2023 statement on AI-generated content are tracked as leads. The 1992 Convention 108 ratification act has no full text in the gazette register; Serbia's party status is taken from the 2010 law amending it, which cites the 1992 act. A follow-up on 22 October 2026 added the June 2024 public-debate draft of the AI strategy as a historical record; the action plan for the 2025-2030 strategy and the AI law remain unpublished.

instruments.official_title: Стратегија развоја вештачке интелигенције у Републици Србији за период 2025–2030. године
instruments.english_title: Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia for the period 2025-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Serbia (prepared on the initiative of the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Government on 10 January 2025 (05 Broj: 011-13287/2024-2) and published in the Službeni glasnik RS no. 5 of 17 January 2025 (gazette text on the state legislation portal: https://pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/reg/viewAct/06df28f0-fa0c-49e0-bd33-a0ed8ed4b882). On entry into force it repealed the 2020-2025 strategy (Sl. glasnik RS 96/19). It provides that an action plan for 2025-2030 is adopted within 90 days and that implementation follows three-year action plans; no adopted action plan was found in the gazette register on 2026-10-13 (see leads). It states that a working group is preparing a Law on Artificial Intelligence (see leads). Also published on the ministry's Strategies page.
instruments.summary: Serbia's second national AI strategy, adopted under the Law on the Planning System, setting objectives and measures to 2030. It aims at a clear institutional and legal framework through a dedicated law regulating the application of AI aligned with international standards, AI education at all levels, support for research and innovation, AI use in the public and private sectors (medicine, biotechnology, education, agriculture, information security) and data governance and open data. It repeals the 2020-2025 strategy; under it, AI training programmes are approved by an AI Council and then accredited or certified.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; announces a dedicated AI law.

instruments.summary: Serbia's first national AI strategy, setting goals and measures so that AI drives economic growth, better public services, scientific capacity and future-oriented skills. It covers five areas: education, science and innovation, an AI-based economy, public-sector services using AI, and the ethical and safe application of AI in line with internationally recognised principles and the EU approach. Public administration, health and transport are named as priority public-sector domains.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI strategy; basis for the National AI Platform, the AI Institute and the 2023 ethics guidelines.

instruments.official_title: Етичке смернице за развој, примену и употребу поуздане и одговорне вештачке интелигенције
instruments.english_title: Ethical Guidelines for the Development, Application and Use of Reliable and Responsible Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Serbia (adopted by Government conclusion on the proposal of the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation)
instruments.publisher_name: Government of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.current_status: Adopted by Government conclusion 05 broj 660-2524/2023-1 of 23 March 2023 and published, with the guidelines annexed as an integral part, in the Službeni glasnik RS no. 23 of 24 March 2023. The conclusion recommends (does not require) that state administration bodies and holders of public powers apply the guidelines when developing, deploying, using or procuring AI systems; application may be limited or excluded for defence and security matters; all other persons are also recommended to apply them. The guidelines document itself is dated February 2023. The National AI Platform page (ai.gov.rs) for the guidelines renders without content.
instruments.summary: Government ethics guidelines for trustworthy and responsible AI, adopted by Government conclusion and recommended to state bodies, holders of public powers (including local government, public enterprises and agencies) and private developers and users, including when procuring AI systems. They define AI systems and high-risk AI systems, set four principles (explainability and verifiability, dignity, prohibition of harm, fairness) and seven conditions for trustworthy AI (human agency and oversight, technical robustness and safety, privacy and data governance, transparency, diversity and non-discrimination, societal and environmental well-being, accountability), each with a yes/no self-assessment checklist and recommendations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national AI ethics instrument and self-assessment checklist pending a dedicated AI law; recommended for public-sector AI use and procurement.

instruments.official_title: Закон о заштити података о личности
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the National Assembly on 9 November 2018, promulgated 13 November 2018 and published in the Službeni glasnik RS no. 87 of 13 November 2018 (gazette text on the state legislation portal). Art. 102: in force on the eighth day after publication (computed 21 November 2018) and applies nine months after entry into force (computed 21 August 2019), except art. 98. A new Draft Law on Personal Data Protection with a chapter on processing by AI systems was put to public debate by the Ministry of Justice from 30 July to 10 September 2026 (recorded separately). A copy of the gazette text is also hosted by the Supreme Court.
instruments.summary: Serbia's GDPR-aligned general data protection law governing processing of personal data, including for AI training and use, enforced by the Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection. Art. 38 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects or significantly affect them, with exceptions (contract, law with safeguards, explicit consent) and minimum safeguards of human involvement, the right to express a view and to contest the decision; arts. 23-24 require information about such automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding national rule on automated decision-making/profiling.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Serbia

instruments.summary: Government decision establishing the Artificial Intelligence Council for five years as an advisory body that coordinates implementation of the national AI strategic framework, monitors AI development and standards, and prepares proposals, recommendations, standards and opinions on all AI questions. It defines and monitors the AI strategy action plan, oversees drafting of the new strategy, and organises and monitors the drafting of laws and by-laws on AI; it is chaired by an adviser to the Prime Minister and supported by the Prime Minister's Cabinet.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 25 July 2024 (05 broj 02-7095/2024), published in the Službeni glasnik RS no. 63 of 26 July 2024; membership amended in no. 75 of 6 September 2024. Point 9: in force on the eighth day after publication (computed 3 August 2024). Point 6: established for five years from entry into force.

instruments.summary: Government founding act of the state-owned Research and Development Institute for Artificial Intelligence of Serbia in Novi Sad, under the Law on Science and Research. Art. 7 tasks the Institute, in line with Government policies, with analysing and monitoring the state of AI, building expertise through research projects, participating in shaping AI public policy, cooperating on AI standardisation and study programmes, and supporting AI solutions for the Serbian language; it sets its governing bodies (managing board and director) and funding.

instruments.official_title: Нацрт закона о заштити података о личности
instruments.english_title: Draft Law on Personal Data Protection (2026)
instruments.summary: Ministry of Justice draft of a new personal data protection law to replace the 2018 law, with a section on processing personal data using AI (arts. 52-53). It allows personal data to be used to develop, test and apply AI systems and general-purpose AI models if compatible with the original purpose or, exceptionally, on legitimate interest, with minimisation and pseudonymisation; it requires a data protection impact assessment and Commissioner opinion for high-risk AI systems, informing people that they are interacting with AI or with emotion recognition or synthetic content, a ban on solely automated AI processing that may harm or significantly affect a person, and labelling of AI-generated or modified audio and video content.
instruments.current_status: Public debate held from 30 July to 10 September 2026 on the eKonsultacije portal (Ministry of Justice notice), with a round table on 7 September 2026; the report on the public debate was posted on the portal on 25 September 2026. Not yet submitted to the National Assembly as a bill on 2026-10-13. Draft art. on entry into force: eighth day after publication in the Službeni glasnik.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding-law text with explicit AI provisions (AI risk tiers, transparency, synthetic-content labelling) at draft stage.

instruments.english_title: Draft Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia for the period 2024-2030 (public debate, June 2024)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
instruments.current_status: Draft posted for public debate by the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation in June 2024 (file in the ministry's 13 June 2024 news folder); the text leaves the debate dates blank. Superseded by the Strategy for 2025-2030, adopted by the Government on 10 January 2025 (Službeni glasnik RS 5/2025).
instruments.summary: Public-debate draft of Serbia's second national AI strategy, prepared by a working group founded on 12 December 2023 for adoption by the Government under the Law on the Planning System. It sets a vision of AI for economic and scientific progress and citizens' wellbeing and six goals: education and promotion, a legal and institutional framework, support for AI development, wider adoption across society and the economy, data as a key resource, and infrastructure. Planned measures include an AI law and bylaws led by the Ministry of Justice, a body responsible for AI matters and a body for data management.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Consultation version of the strategy that became the 2025-2030 AI Development Strategy; records the first official proposal of a Serbian AI law and an AI body.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Serbia's official legislation register, parliament, the public consultation portal, each ministry and the sector regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for cybersecurity, sandboxes, readiness indices, sectoral rules or international agreements. The health, justice and agriculture ministry sites, the scanned Criminal Code amendment bills, a media regulator statement on AI-generated content and the original 1992 Convention 108 ratification act are still to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). Shared web-search limit hit mid-run: NBS, RATEL, REM, competition and cyber authorities, ministries of health, justice, defence, finance, labour, interior, standards body, Public Procurement Office, eKonsultacije not reached. Ethics guidelines primary_source_located (ai.gov.rs content empty; date from Government statement 23 Mar 2023). Gazette issue numbers unconfirmed for 2025-2030 strategy, action plan and guidelines. Data protection law read from gazette copy hosted by the Supreme Court (vrh.sud.rs, state body); publication 2018-11 (issue date not printed); effective 2019-08-21 computed from art. 102. Action Plan 2020-2022 set to adopted (period ended, no successor). Convention 108: party (Sl. list SRJ - Međunarodni ugovori 1/92 per Commissioner) but act not readable - added to pending_c108. Thin pass 2026-10-13: gazette register searched via di.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/REG/advancedSearch (POST), full texts from reg.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/api/viewAct (used as source_url; portal page as official_webpage_url); eKonsultacije topic API (673 topics); ISS catalogue. i-2c66f733d52b publication_date 2025-01-10 -> 2025-01-17 (Sl. glasnik RS 5/2025). i-fa67bbad2f6f now reviewed from gazette (Government conclusion 23/2023 of 2023-03-24), title now Cyrillic. i-4b96a9579e72 re-sourced to gazette text, publication 2018-11-13. Added AI Council decision (63/2024, 75/2024; in force 2024-08-03), AI Institute founding decision (24/2021), draft data protection law 2026 (arts 52-53; consultation 2026-07-30), SRPS ISO/IEC 42001:2025, 23894:2023, 22989:2023 (located only, catalogue entries). Convention 108: 2010 amending law (Sl. glasnik RS - MU 12/2010) read, original 1/92 act not; used as the Convention 108 source (1992 act not read); removed from pending_c108. Not reached: health, justice, agriculture ministry sites; scanned bills; REM statement text. Units covered: Law: Official gazette / legislation portal (pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs): its register search API was used directly (title and body searches in Cyrillic for AI terms and automated decision-making). Found and recorded: AI Council decision (63/2024), AI Institute founding decision (24/2021), ethics guidelines conclusion (23/2023, full text), 2025-2030 strategy (5/2025), Law on Personal Data Protection (87/2018, gazette text). No AI-specific law; no deepfake offence, public-sector algorithm or AI procurement rule found in force. General acts with passing AI mentions (Law on Ministries, Consumer Protection Law 2026, science, data-protection, e-communications, information-society, education and PAR strategies, customs e-systems plan, education rulebooks, international MoUs) held as leads or noted. Commissioner DPIA list decision (automated decisions/profiling) held as a lead.; Parliament: parlament.gov.rs bills in procedure (101 bills, all pages): no AI bill and no data-protection bill pending; three Criminal Code amendment bills and one Electronic Media bill are scanned PDFs with no extractable text and no AI reference found by search.; Government: Ministry of Science (nitra.gov.rs Strategies page): both AI strategies and the 2020-2022 action plan re-checked; no 2025-2030 action plan published. ai.gov.rs scanned (ethics page still empty; guidelines now read from the gazette). eKonsultacije (all 673 topics): found the Ministry of Justice Draft Law on Personal Data Protection with an AI chapter (recorded), the proposed e-Government Programme 2026-2030 (lead), the 2024 draft AI strategy and 2022 draft ethics guidelines consultations (superseded by adopted texts). No AI law draft. No public-sector GenAI guideline or AI procurement rule found.; Ministries: Education (incl. higher education): no ministry AI guidance; ZUOV (Institute for the Improvement of Education) published on 26 June 2026 only an informational Serbian summary of the OECD/EC AI literacy framework (not a national document); education rulebooks mention AI in curricula only. Health: nothing found (gazette search and site check; zdravlje.gov.rs not reachable). Justice: Draft Law on Personal Data Protection 2026 (recorded). Defence: nothing found (mod.gov.rs search page 404; gazette nothing). Finance/tax: customs e-systems work plan 2025-2029 mentions AI as a tool (internal plan, not recorded); mfin.gov.rs and purs.gov.rs no AI documents. Labour: nothing found. Interior: Draft Law on Processing Personal Data in Internal Affairs (2026) read, no AI provisions (lead). Agriculture: nothing found (minpolj.gov.rs not reachable; gazette strategy only passing). Foreign affairs: only AI cooperation MoUs (UAE, Italy, Czech Republic etc.) in the gazette treaty series; not national governance documents. Public administration: e-Government programme proposal (lead). Information and telecommunications: no AI document (only e-communications and information-security acts).; Regulators: Commissioner for Personal Data Protection: no AI guidance or decision found (site search 404, web search nothing); DPIA list decision held as lead. National Bank of Serbia: no AI rule found in gazette-published NBS acts or by web search. Securities Commission (sec.gov.rs): nothing found. RATEL (telecoms, also national CERT): no AI document; its 2026 ICT risk-assessment methodology rulebook does not mention AI. REM (media): August 2023 statement on AI-generated content reported in press but not found on rem.rs (lead). Commission for Protection of Competition (kzk.gov.rs): nothing found. ALIMS (medicines and medical devices): nothing found. National Accreditation Body / higher-education accreditation (nat.gov.rs): nothing found. Public Procurement Office (ujn.gov.rs): nothing found. Institute for Standardization of Serbia: SRPS ISO/IEC 42001:2025, 23894:2023 and 22989:2023 recorded; further adoptions (42005:2026, 42006:2026, TR 24027/24028/24368, CEN/CLC TR 17894) exist in the ISS catalogue.. Not reached: Ministry of Health website (zdravlje.gov.rs: connection failed); Ministry of Justice website (mpravde.gov.rs: connection failed; its draft law read via eKonsultacije); Ministry of Agriculture website (minpolj.gov.rs: connection failed); Full text of three Criminal Code amendment bills and an Electronic Media amendment bill on parlament.gov.rs (scanned image PDFs); REM statement of August 2023 on AI-generated content (official text not located). Could not verify: Convention 108 ratification act of 1992 (Sl. list SRJ - MU 1/92): register entry exists without full text on pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs.; Content of the scanned Criminal Code amendment bills on parlament.gov.rs (no text layer), so possible deepfake provisions could not be checked.; REM August 2023 statement on AI-generated content (only press reports found).; Gazette references for the 2020-2025 strategy (96/19 as cited) and the 2020-2022 action plan: not in the current register (repealed or not listed).. cyber-security, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): Three Criminal Code bills and an electronic media bill are scanned without text, so possible deepfake provisions could not be checked, and the health, justice and agriculture ministries' sites could not be accessed.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The health, justice and agriculture ministry sites were unavailable, and the scanned Deep review wave 4, 2026-10-22: the session proxy refused curl connections to pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs, srbija.gov.rs, mit.gov.rs, poverenik.rs and ite.gov.rs (CONNECT 403); WebFetch read PDFs on nitra.gov.rs, ite.gov.rs and nbs.rs. Added the June 2024 public-debate draft of the AI strategy 2024-2030 as a historical consultation record (promotes the lead). No 2025-2030 action plan, AI law draft, Commissioner AI guidance, NBS AI rule or REM statement text found; the NBS 2017 IT-system standards decision carries no AI provision. The e-Government Programme 2026-2030 remains a proposal (consultation report on mduls.gov.rs).

Record as consultation_draft once a draft is published. 2026-10-22: no draft published on eKonsultacije or the ministry's site.

leads.note: Public debate on eKonsultacije (topic 456; Government conclusion posted 30 March 2026). Not yet in the gazette register on 2026-10-13; consider a public-sector record once adopted if its AI measures are substantive. 2026-10-22: the ministry's consultation report is posted on mduls.gov.rs; no adopted programme in the gazette register.

leads.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Serbia
leads.note: Sl. glasnik RS 84/2026 (9 September 2026), read on the legislation portal (https://pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/reg/viewAct/51922f59-41e8-4489-a256-9f6b042f5238). AI is one of several priority research areas and measure 1.5 sets up a national plan for computing capacity for science and AI; a general science strategy, not AI-specific, so held as a lead.

Discusses AI as a data-protection challenge in its analysis but sets no AI-specific measure; its action plans 2023-2024 and 2025-2027 were consulted on eKonsultacije.

leads.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia
leads.note: Law on Ministries (Sl. glasnik RS 128/2020, 116/2022, 92/2023), read on the legislation portal (https://pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/reg/viewAct/4cd2d833-d371-4ca1-a802-e998bae79a3b): assigns the Ministry of Science 'proposing and implementing policy and programmes in the field of AI' and assigns preparing data for developing AI systems by state bodies. leads.english_title: Commissioner's Decision on the list of processing operations requiring a data protection impact assessment and the Commissioner's opinion
leads.issuing_authority: Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection
leads.note: Sl. glasnik RS 45/2019 and 112/2020, read on the legislation portal (https://pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/reg/viewAct/2d4572ae-5f31-4e70-af53-78eb82f92ff5). Binding list requiring a DPIA for systematic automated evaluation and profiling with significant effects, profiling or automated decisions on children or special-category data, and new technologies for analysing or predicting behaviour. Does not mention AI by name, so held as a lead; could be added as a data-privacy/risk-assurance record if the lead reviewer treats automated decision-making rules as in scope.
